text:
Maya: quick update from this morning's KV quant runs (FP8 vs INT8) on redwood-13b-v2 — ran prod-profile latency+mem sweep across gpu:a100-80gb, batch sizes 1/8, seq=1024 + 8k KV cache. results below.

Jihoon: TL;DR: FP8KV gives best tail latency, INT8KV gives biggest steady-state mem wins but shows cold-start jitter in a few cases. numbers: p50/p95 (bs=1, seq=1024, ctx=8kKV):
- fp16 baseline: p50=36ms, p95=76ms, KV mem=48.0GB/shard
- FP8-KV: p50=33ms, p95=62ms, KV mem=24.5GB/shard (-49%)
- INT8-KV: p50=34ms, p95=68ms, KV mem=18.9GB/shard (-60.6%)

Sam: important nuance: cold-start (first request after container spin) p95: fp16=420ms, FP8=360ms, INT8=660ms on a subset of runs where the INT8 kernel forced a fallback + cache rebuild. that explains tail spikes.

Priya: accuracy check vs fp16 baseline on our eval sets (SQuAD-like QA + internal convo evals):
- FP8-KV: small deltas, QA EM -0.23% abs, conv-quality metric -0.18%
- INT8-KV: QA EM -0.65% abs, conv-quality -0.5% (worst in corner cases with very long contexts and repeated prompts)
notes: differences are stable across 5 seeds, artifacts concentrated on numeric stability in attention logits when kv entries are large.

Maya: reproducible run commands i used:
```
# run (single process)
perf-run --model redwood-13b-v2 --device gpu:a100-80gb --quant kv:fp8 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --kv-cache 8192 --profile prod --run-id fp8-kv-1968
perf-run --model redwood-13b-v2 --device gpu:a100-80gb --quant kv:int8 --batch 1 --seq 1024 --kv-cache 8192 --profile prod --run-id int8-kv-1968
```

Maya: config snippet we rolled locally for the FP8 pilot (feature flag + warmup):
```
{"route":"/chat/generate","quant_kv":"fp8","kv_warmup_requests":4,"cache_prefetch":true}
```

Jihoon: perf-bot run metadata: run-id=fp8-kv-1968, commit=rev@a1b2c3, p95=62ms, kv_mem=24.5GB, accuracy_delta=-0.23%. for int8 run-id=int8-kv-1968 commit=rev@a1b2c3 p95=68ms kv_mem=18.9GB accuracy_delta=-0.65%

perf-bot: job fp8-kv-1968 completed (logs: s3://redwood-perf/1968765432/fp8-kv-1968.tar.gz)

Sam: deployment suggestion:
- route-level policy: enable FP8-KV for latency-sensitive routes (chat, assistant) with kv_warmup_requests=3
- enable INT8-KV for high-throughput batch or embedding-like workloads where mem savings > tolerable accuracy delta
- add fallback policy: if tail p95 > 2x baseline for 10m, automatically revert to fp16 for that instance and flag for ops review

Priya: also recommend adding a small eval harness to the rollout that runs the 200-sample regression set after deploy and blocks on >0.5% QA EM regression (auto rollback).

Maya: next steps: Jh to add FP8 route flag + rollout plan, Sam to add warmup default in runtime, Priya to formalize eval harness. i'll start a canary for /chat/generate tomorrow 09:00 PDT with ~2% traffic.

Jihoon: acked. will add instrumentation to capture cold-start vs warm tail separately (we need to know percent of requests hitting cold cache).

Sam: FYI i put a short note in the run logs about the INT8 dequant fallback pattern: stack traces show kernel "kv_dequantize_v2" calling fallback path ~30% of the time on long-context ops. logs in s3.

Maya: thanks — moving this to the FP8 pilot doc. cc @ops-team for canary schedule. :rocket:
